hook.text: Farmed fish now outnumber wild-caught fish for the first time—aquaculture produces over 50% of seafood we eat.

buildup.text: Fish, shrimp, and seaweed farms can produce protein more efficiently than land-based livestock.

discovery.text: Offshore aquaculture moves farms to the open ocean—reducing coastal pollution and disease risks.

twist.text: Badly managed fish farms pollute with antibiotics, excess feed, and escaped fish that outcompete wild populations.

climax.text: Seaweed farming may be the most sustainable option—no feed, no freshwater, absorbs CO₂ and nitrogen.

punchline.text: Farming the sea could feed the world—if we do it right.

quiz.question: What percentage of seafood now comes from aquaculture?
